title: [grid/kanban] Four class-string-only badge call sites still quantize the author's declared hex, so one option colour now renders two different ways depending on the surface
body:
Follow-up to objectui#5141, filed from that card's implementation. Not fixed there: #5141's ruled file surface was `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` plus its tests, and these call sites live in other packages.

## What #5141 changed

`SelectCellRenderer` now renders an explicitly declared `options[].color` hex as declared, for both `appearance: 'badge'` and `appearance: 'dot'`, instead of bucketing it into one of nine palette families. The colours are carried as CSS custom properties consumed by static Tailwind utilities, exposed by two new helpers in `@object-ui/fields`:

- `getBadgeHexAppearance(color)` returns `{ className, style }` or `undefined`
- `getDotHexAppearance(color)` likewise

## What still quantizes

`getBadgeColorClasses(color, val)` returns only a class string, so it cannot carry a runtime colour — Tailwind can never generate a class for a value that is not in the source at build time. It was deliberately left behaviour-identical in #5141 so no consumer regressed. The consequence is that these four call sites still snap the declared hex to a family:

- `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` — the compact card/mobile stage badge
- `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx` — `resolveGroupHeader`, the group-header pills
- `packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx` — two call sites

## Why this is worth fixing rather than leaving

The grid's own comment says the card view matches the desktop grid "via getBadgeColorClasses". After #5141 that is no longer true: the desktop cell honours the declared hex and the compact card does not. So the same option, in the same object, renders one colour in a grid cell and a different one in the group header above it or the Kanban card beside it. The pre-#5141 state was at least uniformly wrong; this is non-uniform, which is harder for an author to reason about.

The fix is mechanical — at each site, prefer `getBadgeHexAppearance(color)` when it returns a value and pass its `className` plus `style`, falling back to `getBadgeColorClasses` otherwise, exactly as `SelectCellRenderer` does. Both packages already depend on `@object-ui/fields`.

Worth deciding as part of it: whether `getBadgeColorClasses` should stay class-only forever, or whether the four sites should move to a single shared helper so a fifth caller cannot reintroduce the split.

## Not in scope here

The quantizer itself (`hexToPaletteName`) stays — `getSemanticColorName` still returns family names and `plugin-gantt` depends on that.
